purpose: Source port of callback-thread MaterialPtr info strong ownership and static concrete-class joins; not scene/GPU ownership
staticInterpretation: The vertex/fragment/geometry path keys identify the concrete parseShader virtual slot; both selected parsers write the adjacent 0xd0/0xf0/0x110 fields
Another current parser at 0x5a4f600 uses the same names/fields but belongs to another vtable group. Concrete-class table pointers, not names alone, select 0x4df5f50 at 0xf2147e0 slot 4
Both traced info loaders allocate 0x58 bytes, initialize strong/weak counts at control+8/+12, place the info object at control+0x10 and store object/control as the MaterialPtr pair

The concrete control table has destroy/delete/deleting-destructor entries. Destroy tears down the info-owned unique pointer and name/weak metadata; delete calls the deleting destructor with flag 1; the latter frees exactly 0x58 bytes
General borrowed MaterialPtr observation still permits aliasing pairs. Only the retained skinned-info path requires the inspected concrete allocation relation and table

Full normalized matches for the selected old loader, info destroy and path parser failed; independent construction, class-table and operand witnesses are retained instead of claiming whole-function identity
sourceBehavior: Acquisition is unsafe and requires a live strong pair owned by the active native constructor/submission callback. Readable memory or positive counts do not supply this contract
The source checks the exact control class and three rebased method pointers, then attempts at most 32 SeqCst compare-exchanges on a live positive aligned strong count without overflow or resurrection
Drop releases exactly the acquired strong count; last strong invokes the pinned destroy routine and drops its implicit weak count; last weak invokes the pinned native delete routine
An invalid release count latches future acquisition/current checks off. This is diagnostic handling, not proof against an external lifetime-contract violation
The retained owner is !Send/!Sync via PhantomData<Rc<()>> and remains in the existing thread-local synchronous pending/material consumer scopes
SkinnedMaterial retains info before shader/variation copying, then rechecks its copied MaterialPtr/pointee metadata and retained control before admitting replay material inputs
Unsafe lifetime requirements propagate from the actual native description constructor callback through observation, replay preparation and material copying
Only material path fingerprints/scalars leave the callback. No native owner is sent to archive, upload/retire workers or world geometry packets

Pending reset, scope retirement, rejected preparation and consumer overflow move retained entries out of RefCell borrows before dropping them, so a last-reference engine destructor does not run under the observer's mutable state borrow
The nested unique_ptr may be replaced while its info remains alive; the retained info is therefore not presented as a RenderMaterial, descriptor, scene-target or GPU lifetime lease
